subject: Expedited MAP: cost gating & token economics playbook

Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation & timeline (intro + MAP)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement is asking for a short mutual action plan and a specific breakdown on cost assumptions (tokens/$, recommended batching and caching) so we can include it in our vendor packet and run a quick cost sensitivity exercise.

High level asks from Plexa procurement:
- Targeted tokens/month for pilot (we expect 25M tokens)
- Expected tokens per user and per call (chat vs embed)
- Baseline tokens/$ and examples of how caching/batching shifts that metric
- Any minimum commit or reserved capacity needed for predictable latency at 99p

Can your team provide a 1-page MAP section and an attached spreadsheet with model assumptions by EOD Monday (PST)? Also cc'ing our procurement inbox: procurement@plexahealth.com.

—Megan

Folks — looping you in to build the MAP + unit-econ workbook. Procurement wants concise artifacts for a quick internal review. Goal: deliver a MAP section + unit-econ spreadsheet Monday EOD PST.

Quick plan (suggested split):
- Karthik: run token profiling for the demo prompts + build baseline tokens/$ rows (gpt-style per-token throughput with current Redwood hosted price bands). Include how quantization and model variant (smaller vs medium) change tokens/$ for same 1k-token convo.
- Monica: draft the MAP language (owners, milestones, acceptance criteria) and capture required procurement artifacts (SOC2, data residency statement).
- Sean: provide latency SLO/commit guidance and quick reserved-capacity sizing for 25M tokens/month pilot plus 2x burst. Include impact of batching on 95/99p latency.

Key economics checks to include in the workbook (short):
1) Tokens-per-dollar baseline (hosted) — show raw token cost and effective tokens/$ after 1) cache hits and 2) batching.
2) Caching assumptions — prefix cache hit-rate scenarios (0%, 20%, 50%) with examples of user flows that drive those hits.
3) Batching assumptions — average request size, target latency SLOs, and how batch windows affect unit cost vs p99 latency.
4) Sensitivity rows — worst/likely/best-case tokens/$ for pilot and steady-state.

Attachments: I created a stub workbook (unit-econ-sheet.xlsx) and a MAP template (sample-map-template.pdf) in Drive — add your inputs. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPPLAYBOOK

Tight timeline: draft by Mon 06/18 11:00 PST for internal review, final to customer by EOD 06/18. If you need more time we push to 06/20 but procurement prefers earlier.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

On Thu, Jun 14, 2028 at 09:05 AM Vivek wrote:
> Folks — looping you in to build the MAP + unit-econ workbook. Procurement wants concise artifacts for a quick internal review. Goal: deliver a MAP section + unit-econ spreadsheet Monday EOD PST.

Quick numbers from my side — rough, will populate spreadsheet:
- Demo prompts: avg 280 tokens per chat interaction, 1.8 calls/user/day for our pilot persona -> ~151M tokens/month if 100k users (but their ask is 25M pilot). I modeled both.
- Baseline hosted token cost (current public band): $0.0008 per token (model M), so baseline tokens/$ ~= 1,250 tokens per $1.
- Quantized smaller model variant (model S) shows ~3x tokens/$ improvement for short-turn use cases but may increase hallucination risk for longer context.
- Caching: with a 20% prefix hit-rate and 50% token reduction on cache-hit responses, effective tokens/$ improves ~18%. At 50% hit-rate we see ~40% improvement.
- Batching: for short chat calls, batching windows of 25–50ms improve GPU utilization but add ~10–30ms to median latency; this can reduce per-token GPU cost by ~12% in our testing.

I'll drop the populated sheet into Drive and add a small sensitivity table (worst/likely/best). Will flag where model variant tradeoffs are material.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP deliverables & timeline — Plexa pilot (DEAL-4721)

Megan / procurement —

Quick update and delivery plan per your request. Attached: unit-econ-sheet.xlsx (populated with baseline, caching/batching scenarios, model-variant rows) and a 1-page MAP excerpt placed in Drive (link below).

Summary highlights (one-liners):
- Pilot scope: 25M tokens/month target, 3-week ramp.
- Baseline tokens/$: ~1,250 tokens per $1 (model M, hosted).
- With conservative caching (20% hit-rate) + modest batching (25ms window) the effective tokens/$ improves ~20% — we included sensitivity bands for 0/20/50% cache and batching latency choices.
- Recommended path to preserve latency SLOs: start hosted with reserved capacity sized for 25M tokens/month + 2x burst; evaluate quantized model S on a subset of traffic for cost savings after functional eval.

Next steps / asks for Plexa:
1) Confirm pilot tokens/month target and expected 95/99p latency requirement.
2) Share a short list of three typical user flows for prefix-caching analysis (e.g., order lookup, triage question, intake form).
3) Sign off on MAP milestones: kickoff (06/25), pilot launch (07/16), pilot review (08/06).

Links/attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPPLAYBOOK, HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/4721

If you want we can run a short internal cost-sensitivity walkthrough before you share with procurement — happy to set a 30m call next week.

Best — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
